description_en: Here, in violation of the Archaeological Act, a historicpāṭīhas been removed and modified, and the addition of new concrete structures has caused thepīṭhaprecinct to appear constricted.Caṇḍeśvarī is worshipped as the tutelary goddess of Tokha, or theAjimāof the settlement. Herdyaḥchẽis located within the settlement at Thalāga Ṭola (TOK0090), while thepīṭhais situated approximately 1.5 km to the north. Thispīṭhahouses not only Goddess Caṇḍeśvarī but also a temple of Caṇḍeśvara Mahādeva. Late Medieval inscriptions found here mention the name and eulogy of Caṇḍeśvara Mahādeva alongside Caṇḍeśvarī, indicating that Mahādeva has been established here since that period. InŚāktatradition, the establishment of a Śivaliṅga in the name of Caṇḍeśvara rather than Bhairava alongside Caṇḍeśvarī in her Cāmuṇḍā form is an unusual and noteworthy practice. Dozens of ropanīs of land have been left as an open field in the name of Caṇḍeśvarī. We find similar open spaces dedicated to other Mother Goddesspīṭhaswithin the valley. In the midst of this open field, the structure of thepīṭhafaces north. In the year 2006 AD (VS 2063), the tree was removed and a temple was erected over the pedestal that used to be at the base of a former large tree. Thepīṭhacontains an aniconic stone worshipped as Caṇḍeśvarī. Five layers oftoraṇashave been offered in a tiered arrangement oriented toward this stone. Among these five, thetoraṇaon the third level includestvalaṃthāṃ(the supporting posts of thetoraṇa) and was installed during the decade of 810s NS. Standing statues of Gaṇeśa and Kumāra are carved on its left and right, while the iconic form of Caṇḍeśvarī, or Cāmuṇḍā, is carved on the upper part of thetoraṇa. Thetoraṇaabove this level is even more magnificent and was installed during the decade of 800s NS. This stonetoraṇadisplays the iconic form ofAṣṭamātṛkā. At the entrance to thepīṭhacourtyard, which houses these tieredtoraṇastructures, there is another stonetoraṇa. Thistoraṇaalso features carved figures of theŚāktagaṇa. A pair of stone lions, installed in 1688 CE (NS 808), flank thistoraṇa. Upon examining the iconographic characteristics of the Caṇḍeśvarī statues found here, they represent Cāmuṇḍā, or Kālī.Although numerous inscriptions in the valley mention the offering of stone items such astoraṇas, lions, and thrones topīṭhas, no inscription has been found that mentions the construction of thepīṭhaitself. It appears that suchpīṭhasevolved through the gradual addition of artistic objects over aniconic stones, particularly those located in cremation grounds. Here too, about half a dozen Late Medieval inscriptions mentioning the addition of various objects to thepīṭhahave been found. During the latter part of the Malla period, the residents of Tokha seemingly beautified thepīṭhaby adding various stone objects to please theirAjimā. However, in the Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī it is mentioned that during the reign of Ratna Malla, around NS 629-30, a town of 300 houses was built for the protection of the theKuṃkuṃcalled Bhotes (Tibetan groups), and Caṇḍeśvarī was established during this process (N. Yogī VS 2013, p. 96). However, the discovery of Licchavi inscriptions from the Śivadeva-Aṃśuvarma period in Tokha confirms that the settlement existed at that time (D. Vajrācārya VS 2036, p. 266). Similarly, the Gopālarājavaṃśāvalī mentions certain events that occurred in Tokha as early as the century of NS 300 (Gopālarājavaṃśāvalī fol. 37). *From this, the description of the Ratna Malla period in the Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī does not appear to be credible. An inscription has been found mentioning that Padmāvatī, the sister of Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha, built a phalcā in thepīṭhaarea. It is interesting and notable that she built a phalcā at the Tokhapīṭha. She was likely married into a noble family of the Tokha region. The location, which was a meadow, used to have a pīṭha, the temple of Caṇḍeśvara Mahādeva, and a few phalcās. Following the recent earthquake, various concrete structures added here have made the open space appear cramped. In the past, there was a custom of releasing live male goats and sheep in the name of Caṇḍeśvarī in the open field here. These animals would graze here, reproduce, and increase in number (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 59).The Karmācārya family of Tokha has been performing the daily worship and maintenance at both the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha and thedyaḥchẽ. While it is common elsewhere to find Karmācāryas at thedyaḥchẽinside the settlement and theDyālācommunity at thepīṭha, a different system is observed here where the Karmācārya clan oversees thepīṭhaas well.The influence of Bhaktapur is clearly visible in the language and culture of the Tokha residents. Like in Bhaktapur, a festival is celebrated in Tokha during Caitra-Vaiśākha under the name Biskāḥjātrā. At midday on the last day of Caitra, the metal idol is taken out of Caṇḍeśvarī’s dyaḥchẽ (TOK0090) in Thalāga Ṭola and placed on a ceremonial palanquin (khaṭ). After worship in front of thedyaḥchẽ, the ceremonial palanquin is brought to thispīṭha. The idol is placed on a throne atop the aniconic stone of thepīṭha, a ritual known asdyaḥ gamay taygu. Here, a large-scale state-sponsored worship is conducted withpañcavali(sacrifice of five types of animals), followed by a feast. The next day, on the 1st of the month at midday, the ceremonial palanquin is brought to Tokha, and the festival is celebrated grandly by circumambulating the Tokha town until the 4th. On the 4th, the idol is taken back inside thedyaḥchẽand enshrined. While the festival of a settlement's tutelary goddess usually occurs only once a year, an exception is found here and in Sunaguthi, where the custom of celebrating twojātrāsa year exists. Here, there is a tradition of holding ajātrāon the bright fortnight day of Kārtika as well, placing both Caṇḍeśvarī and Caṇḍeśvara Mahādeva on the same ceremonial palanquin. A distinct feature observed at thispīṭhais the custom of newlywed couples visiting for kalaḥpūjā on the fourth day of their marriage. It is a popular belief that this worship is performed with the aim of inspiring procreation by viewing the depictions of erotic art (kāmakalā) in the Caṇḍeśvara temple adjacent to thepīṭha(M. Śreṣṭha VS 2075, p. 87).Historical Notes:*On the day of fourteenth day of Āśvina, 1254 CE (NS 374), King Jayadeva of Bhvanta (Banepā) captured and took the gold located at Nepīkvāṭha and Tokhākvāṭha, causing this place to rebel.*In the time of 1255 CE (NS 375), while Śrī Abhaya Malladeva was ruling, a massive earthquake occurred, and one-third of the population, including the King, died.
description_ne: यहाँ पुरातात्विक ऐन विपरित ऐतिहासिक पाटी हटाई सम्याउने कार्य भएको छ भने कंक्रिडका नयाँ संरचनाहरू थपिएकाले पीठ परिसर साँघुरिएको देखापर्छ ।तोखाकी आरध्यदेवी अर्थात् बस्तीकी अजिमाका रूपमा चण्डेश्वरीलाई पुजिन्छ । उनको द्यःछेँ बस्तीभित्र (TOK0090) थलाग टोलमा छ भने पीठ बस्तीबाट करिब १.५ किमीको दूरीमा उत्तरतिर अवस्थित छ (google map) । यस पीठमा चण्डेश्वरी देवीमात्र नभई उनको साथमा चण्डेश्वर महादेवको पनि मन्दिर छ । उत्तरमध्यकालीन यहाँका अभिलेखहरूमै चण्डेश्वरीसँग-सगै चण्डेश्वर महादेवको पनि नाम र प्रशस्ति परेबाट यहाँ सो समयदेखि महादेव स्थापित थिए भनी थाहा हुन्छ । पीठमा चामुण्डा स्वरूपकी चण्डेश्वरीका साथमा भैरव नभई चण्डेश्वरका नाममा शिवलिङ्ग स्थापित हुनु शाक्त परम्परामा रोचक अभ्यासका रूपमा लिन सकिन्छ । चण्डेश्वरीको नाममा यहाँ दर्जनौं रोपनी जग्गा खुल्ला चौर (ख्यः) का रूपमा छाडिएको छ । उपत्यकाभित्र अन्य मातृका पीठमा पनि यसै गरी खुलाफाँट छाडिएको पाउँछौ । यहाँ खुला चौरमाझ पीठको संरचना उत्तराभिमुख छ । विगत विशाल रूखको फेदीमा हुने गरेको पीठमाथि विसं २०६३ (सन् २००६) मा रूख हटाई मन्दिर उठाइएको हो । पीठमा चण्डेश्वरीका रूपमा पुजिने अमूर्त ढुङ्गा छ । चण्डेश्वरी मानिने उक्त ढुङ्गालाई लक्षित गरी तहगत रूपमा पाँचवटा तोरणका चढाइएका छन् । ती पाँचमध्ये तेस्रो तहको तोरण त्वलंथां (तोरणलाई थमाइने थामो) सिहितको हो जुन नेसं ८१० को दशकमा चढाइएको थियो । यसको दायाँबायाँ गणेश र कुमारका स्थानक मूर्ति कुँदिएका छन् भने तोरणको उचो भागमा चण्डेश्वरी अर्थात् चामुण्डाको मूर्तरूप कुँदिएको छ । यो तहमाथिको तोरण अझ भव्य छ जुन नेसं ८०० को दशकमा चढाइएको थियो । ढुङ्गाको यस तोरणमा अष्टमातृकाका मूर्त रूप देखाइएका छन् । यी तहगत तोरणको संरचना भएको पीठ प्राङ्गणमा प्रवेश गर्ने द्वारमा अर्को एक ढुङ्गे तोरण छ । यस तोरणमा पनि शाक्तगणका मूर्तरूप कुँदिएका छन् । यस तोरणको दायाँ-बयाँ शिलाको एकजोडा सिंहमूर्ति छ जुन नेसं ८०८ (सन् १६८८) मा चढाइएको थियो । यहाँ प्राप्त चण्डेश्वरीका मूर्तिहरूका प्रतिमालक्षण नियाल्दा यिनी चामुण्डा अर्थात् काली हुन् ।उपत्यकाका पीठमा तोरण, सिंह, सिंहासन जस्ता ढुङ्गाका सामग्री चढाइएको प्रसंग परेका थुप्रै अभिलेख पाइए तापनि पीठै निर्माण गरेको प्रसंग परेको अभिलेख कतै पाइएको छैन । खासगरी मसानक्षेत्रमा भएको कुनै अमूर्त ढुङ्गामाथि क्रमिक रूपमा कलात्मक वस्तु थपिँदै गई यस्ता पीठको उद्विकास भएको देखिन्छ । यहाँ पनि पीठमा विविध वस्तु थपिएका प्रसंग परेका करिब आधा दर्जन उत्तरमध्यकालीन अभिलेख प्राप्त छन् । मल्लकालको उत्तरार्धमा खासगरी तोखावासीले आफ्नो अजिमालाई प्रसन्न पार्न विविध ढुङ्गाका वस्तु थपी पीठलाई सौन्दरीकरण गर्दै लगेको देखिन्छ । देवमाला वंशावलीमा भने कुंकुं कहलिने भोटेहरूको सुरक्षाका खातिर रत्नमल्लको शासनकाल अर्थात् नेसं ६२९-३० तिर ३०० घर भएको नगर निर्माण गरेको र यसै दौरान चण्डेश्वरी स्थापना गरेको भाव परेको छ (N. Yogī VS 2013, p. 96) । तोखामा शिवदेव-अंशुवर्माकालीन लिच्छवि अभिलेख पाइएबाट सो समयमै बस्ती भएको पुष्टि हुन्छ (D. Vajrācārya VS 2036, p. 266) । त्यसैगरी गोपालराजवंशावलीमा नेसं ३०० को शदीमै तोखामा घटेका केही घटनाहरूको उल्लेख परेका छन् (Gopālarājavaṃśāvalī fol. 37) ।* यसबाट देवमालावंशावलीको रत्न मल्लकालीन विवसरण विश्वसनीय देखिँदैन । पीठ इलाकामा पृथ्वीनारायण शाहकी बहिनी पद्मावतीले फल्चा बनाएको प्रसंग परेको अभिलेख पाइएको छ । तोखाको पीठमा उनीले फल्चा बनाउनु रोचक र सोचनीय छ । सम्भवतः उनको विवाह तोखा भेगका कुनै कुलघरानासँग भएको थियो । खुला चौरका रूपमा रहेको स्थानमा पीठ, चण्डेश्वर महादेवको मन्दिर र केही फल्चा हुने गर्दथ्यो । पछिल्लो भूकम्प पछि यहाँ थपिएका विविध कंक्रिडका संरचनाले खुला ठाउँ साँघुरिएको देखा पर्छ । विगत यहाँको खुला चौरमा जिउँदा बोका एवं भेडाबाख्रा चण्डेश्वरीका नाममा छाड्ने चलन थियो । यी वस्तु यतै हुर्कने र सन्तानोत्पाद गरी संख्या बढ्दै जाने गर्दथ्यो (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 59) ।चण्डेश्वरीको पीठ र द्यःछेँ दुबै ठाउँमा तोखा निवासी कर्माचार्य परिवारले नित्यपूजा एवं रेखदेखको कार्य गर्दै आएको छ । प्राय अन्त बस्तीभित्रको द्यःछेँमा कर्माचार्य र पीठमा द्यःला समुदायको उपस्थिति पाइन्छ । यहाँ भने पीठमा पनि कर्माचार्य खलकले नै हेर्ने फरक थिति पाइएको छ ।तोखावासीको भाषा एवं संस्कृतिमा भक्तपुरको प्रभाव ज्यादा देख्न सकिन्छ । भक्तपुरमा जस्तै तोखामा पनि बिस्काःजात्राका नामले चैत्र-वैशाखमै जात्रा मनाइन्छ । चैत्र मसान्तको मध्यान्हमा थलाग टोल स्थित चण्डेश्वरीको द्यःछेँ (TOK0090) बाट धातुको मूर्त प्रतिमा निकाली खटमा राखिन्छ । द्यःछेँ अगाडि पूजा पश्चात् खटलाई यस पीठमा ल्याइन्छ । मूर्तिलाई पीठको अमूर्त ढुङ्गामाथि सिंहासनमा राखिन्छ जसलाई ‘द्यः गमय् तय्‌गु’ भनिन्छ । यहाँ पञ्चवली सहित ठुलो स्तरमा सरकारी पूजा सम्पन्न गरी भोज खाने थिति छ । भोलिपल्ट अर्थात् १ गतेको मध्यान्हमा खटलाई तोखा ल्याइन्छ र ४ गतेसम्म तोखा नगरभित्र परिक्रमा गरी भव्य रूपमा जात्रा सम्पन्न गरिन्छ । ४ गते मूर्त प्रतिमालाई द्यःछेँभित्र लगी विराजमान गराइन्छ । बस्तीकी आरध्यदेवीको जात्रा प्राय बस्तीमा प्रतिवर्ष एकपल्ट मात्र हुने गर्दछ । अपवादका रूपमा यहाँ र सुनागुथिमा वर्षको दुईवटा जात्रा मनाउने चलन पाइन्छ छ । यहाँ कार्तिक शुक्ल पूर्णीमाका दिन पनि चण्डेश्वरी र चण्डेश्वर महादेवलाई एकै खटमा राखी जात्र गर्ने थिति छ । यस पीठमा देखिने पृथक विशेषता भनेको नव विवाहिता जोडीले विवाहको चौथो दिन कलःपूजा जाने थिति छ । यो पूजा पीठसँगैको चण्डेश्वर मन्दिरमा भएका कामकलाको चित्रण देखाई सन्तानोत्पादनका खातिर प्रेरित गर्ने लक्षले गरिने लोकमान्यता रही आएको छ (M. Śreṣṭha VS 2075, p. 87)।* नेस ३७४ (सन् १२५४) आश्विन महिनाको चतुर्दशीको दिन भ्वन्त (वनेपा)का राजा जयदेव प्वहले कब्जा गरी नेपीक्वाठ र तोखाक्वाठमा रहेको सुन लिएको हुँदा यस ठाउँले विद्रोह गर्यो |* नेसं ३७५ (सन् १२५५) को समयमा श्री अभय मल्लदेवले शासन गरिरहेको समयमा ठूलो भूकम्प आई राजा समेत ३ भागको १ भाग प्रजा मरे ।

historical_events.event_description: On the southern wall of the circumambulatory path of thepīṭha, there is a sculpture carved on a single stone slab depicting six figures in the gesture of reverence (namaskāra mudrā). This sculpture was installed in the name of Mahādeva and Caṇḍeśvarī. Among the donors’ names, Manisiṃ (Maṇisiṃha) can be read.

On the southern wall of the circumambulatory path of the pīṭha, there is a sculpture carved on a single stone slab depicting six figures in the gesture of reverence (namaskāra mudrā). This sculpture was installed in the name of Mahādeva and Caṇḍeśvarī. Among the donors’ names, Manisiṃ (Maṇisiṃha) can be read.
To please Caṇḍeśvara Mahādeva and Caṇḍeśvarī, one crown, onepira(?), and onepatāsiwere offered. This act of donation was carried out by Viśva Bhāro of Tokha during the reign of Nṛpendra Malla.

During the reign of Bhūpālendra Malla, a pair of stone lion statues was installed at the front of thepīṭha. Among the donors’ names, Sivakinha (Śivakṛṣṇa) and his wife Si_śvarimayi (Siddheśvarī?) can be read.

This inscription is located on thetoraṇapositioned on the upper part of a small stone shrine constructed around the central area where the aniconic stone of the goddess is enshrined at the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha. Apart from the complete date NS 809 recorded in the inscription, the remaining text cannot be clearly read or meaningfully interpreted. Among the names of the donors, Manasiṃ (Manasiṃha) can be read.
The devotees of Tokha built a small stone shrine dedicated to Caṇḍeśvarī, positioning the main stone of thepīṭhaat its center.

This inscription bears a date NS 836 carved at the end of the text. In order to donate thepīṭhawith the intention of seeking liberation for a family member, certain arrangements were made within thepīṭhaprecinct. Written entirely in Sanskrit, the full meaning of this inscription has not been fully deciphered.

This inscription is carved at the feet of the donor figure, indicating that it pertains to the installation of that very statue. Although the date can be read, the remaining letters are no longer legible.

This inscription is preserved inside aphalcāwithin the Caṇḍeśvarī precinct. A trident is carved at the upper part of the inscription, while donor family figures carved in thenamaskāraposture appear in the lower part. Based on its overall characteristics, this inscription can be identified as belonging to the Late Medieval period. However, since all of its letters have been severely eroded, the written information has become unknown.
Due to severe erosion, it has become impossible to comprehend the written information on this inscription. Based on the script, it can be identified as belonging to the Late Malla period.

Padmakumārī, daughter of Narabhūpāla and sister of Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa, commissioned the construction of aphalcāwithin the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha precinct. That the sister of Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa created a work at this location is noteworthy. It is likely that her marital home was in or around Tokha.

The wife of Bhairavasiṃha, a resident of Pukhūlāchi, Tokha, reconstructed a phalcā within the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha precinct that had fallen into a dilapidated state. For its long-term maintenance, aguṭhīwas also established, and annual ritual obligations were prescribed through an inscription.
Ratnamān Śreṣṭha, a resident of Golkhopākhā, Thamel, offered eighty-four bells within thepīṭhaprecinct in the name of his deceased family members.

Centering around thepīṭha, a pillar was erected and a lion statue installed atop it. This act was jointly carried out by Indrarāja Jośī, Prakāaś Maharjan, and Alifa Ḍaṅgol, residents of Tokha, in the names of their respective deceased family members.

Maniṣarāj Jośī offered a metaltoraṇaalong with a pair of flags on the right and left sides atop thepīṭhain the name of his deceased family members.

Maniṣarāj Jośī placed a stone seat bearing his name at the feet of the aniconic stone worshipped as Caṇḍeśvarī. Although no date is mentioned, the donor Maniṣarāj is the same individual who offered the metaltoraṇaand flags here in VS 2078 (2022 CE).
